notes:
Six steps out of eight bullets, and almost all of the judgement is in what is escort technique rather than a rung. The whole sub-tree under bullet 3 -- six Chocobo Blinkers, six Stamina Apples, six Azouph Greens, a few M. Counteragents, and how each one affects the bird -- is shopping advice, not a requirement: every one of those items is bought FROM the Chocobo Tamer at the very step it hangs off, so it cannot be something you must hold to reach that step, and none of it is evidence either, because they are stackable vendor consumables that a player may still be carrying from the last run of a repeatable quest. Holding them proves nothing. Bullet 2 (a Target marker appears on your map) is an outcome of bullet 1, and bullet 5 is a log message plus the recommended route, so both fold into notes.

The page names the destination twice and differently: bullet 4 guides the chocobo to the 'Repair Crate' at (G-7), bullet 6 tells you to click 'the large Repair Trunk'. Both names are kept, the crate on the escort step and the trunk on the click, because the page does not say whether that is one entity written two ways or a crate you walk to beside a trunk you interact with. If one of the two is not a live entity, that step loses its marker and keeps its rung, which is the honest failure; inventing a single reconciled name would not be. Both steps are individually medium for it.

The Chocobo Tamer has no grid of his own -- the page places him only 'near the Resistance Sapper' -- so he inherits (F-9), recorded in his note rather than silently.

The standing line above bullet 1, 'only one Ward Warden / Desert Rain / Crimson Carpet quest can be completed per Vana'dielian day, regardless of Abyssea area', is a real gate on a repeatable quest and nothing in the packets reports Vana'diel days, so it is flagged and modelled nowhere. Fame 'aatt' is an Abyssea zone code and not one of the nine regions, so the region is null and only the raw string survives. The page carries the wiki's own 'unverified' flag, which is why the quest sits at medium rather than high.

steps.note: at Veridical Conflux #00. Bullet 2 is the outcome, not a step: a Target marker then appears on the map showing where the supplies have to go.

speaking to him buys the supplies AND starts the escort. The page grids him only as 'near the Resistance Sapper', so he inherits (F-9). What he sells: at least 6 Chocobo Blinkers (90s, blinker the bird past monsters), 6 Stamina Apples (60s, cuts the HP drain, does not stack with blinkers), at least 6 Azouph Greens (+5% HP, usable only every few minutes) and a few M. Counteragents for the Miasma on the route. All of it is technique, so none of it is recorded as an item.

the tunnel near the Schnitters, NOT Inugami. The bird's HP drains the whole way, and it bolts back to the last safe spot ('Kweh!?' in the log) the moment anything gets line of sight on it -- run back to it and interact to stop it. Recommended route: Stamina Apple immediately, straight north to the dead end, left and slightly north of the AT-04 Martello (Dark Miasma may be up), Silent Oil there or you get ambushed, north hugging the right wall through the rocks, past the AT-06 Martello, then at the Schnitters go to the far wall, turn south and hug it into the tunnel. Silent Oil and Prism Powder on yourself do not break the escort. The name is the conflict described in the quest note.

the large one: click it to gather supplies, then click the chocobo to load them. Selecting 'Depart' closes the loading and starts the return leg. One supply is enough if you only want the completion -- more slows the bird down. This is the object bullet 4 called the 'Repair Crate'; both names are kept, see the quest note.
guide the bird back the way it came -- the page says retracing is the quickest -- and speak to the Tamer to end the escort
Cruor, Resistance Credits and possibly an Empyrean +1 head seal; a reward, so nothing here is evidence

notes:
A clean artifact-armour ladder with two evidence points and a lot of text that is not steps. The header's 'Item Reqs' are the two key items the walkthrough HANDS you -- Valkeng's memory chip at step 2 and the Toggle switch at step 3 -- not things you bring, and they are the quest's only observables; everything after the battle is cutscenes with answers the page says do not matter.

Bullet 2 is not a step. 'You can be any job from here on' is a note on the Puppetmaster gate, which the runtime already handles for free because it only evaluates job gates for quests you have not started, and the sub-bullet about commissioning Dhima Polevhia for three AF pieces is a separate errand whose page is transcluded and therefore not present in this render. Bullets 7, 8 and 9 are a full screen of Valkeng's frame-switching mechanics and party advice; a verb scan would have made three or four steps out of them and every one would have been wrong.

The two key items are carried as the requirement on the Rock Slab rather than on the travel step before it, because the Rock Slab is what actually opens the battlefield. 'Repeatable: af' is the artifact-armour category leaking into the field and means false.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 3: A ??? can never carry a marker, but it keeps the rung and the key item is observable.

steps.note: as a Puppetmaster; the cutscene sends you to his mentor Shamarhaan. Any job from here on. Bullet 2's other half -- commissioning Dhima Polevhia for three AF pieces -- is a side errand, not a rung, and its page is transcluded away.
the chip comes out of his own Automaton; the same cutscene sends you to Mount Zhayolm
On a round steam vent on the ground. Easiest in by Voidwatch warp, then north and left towards the south of the map.

the entrance sits beside the Caedarva Mire Home Point and drops you straight in front of the destination; failing that, the Nashmau Home Point or Survival Guide and the west exit into Caedarva Mire. The two key items are the requirement on the next step, where they are actually used.
north-west of the area; the cutscene puts you into the battlefield. Up to six players, 30 minute limit, Trust Magic allowed inside.

Shamarhaan's old military Automaton. It starts as a Harlequin Frame and re-frames every 30 seconds to whichever damage type has done the most to it -- melee to Valoredge, ranged to Sharpshot, magic to Stormwaker -- and never returns to Harlequin. Bullets 7 to 9 are that mechanic and party advice, not steps. Bullet 10 is the victory cutscene; the answer you pick changes nothing.
another cutscene, and again the answer does not matter
on the docks
the Puppetry Taj is the reward, so it proves the quest is over rather than that a step is done

notes:
Thirteen steps out of fifteen bullets, and the shape is the same loop run twice inside one tower: ??? -> two gargoyle NMs -> the same ??? again -> a coloured door that only opens for the bracelet you just got. That gives three clean evidence points and a ladder that can actually be followed.

Step 1 is the plainest or-branch in the batch. Migliorozz hands over a Phoenix pearl if you have beaten Darkness Named and a Phoenix armlet if you have not, and the page says outright that the quest progresses the same either way. That is exactly what an alternate list is for, so both key items are alternates on the one step and neither is privileged; holding either proves he has been spoken to.

Neither coloured door is named. The page says only 'a blue door' and 'a green door', so both steps keep their rung with a null target rather than a guessed 'Door: ...' name, and each carries its bracelet as the item you must hold -- which is the useful half anyway, since readiness looks at what you hold. The page's own warning that the blue and green door lights can look alike on some screen settings is kept on the blue door where it was written.

'Quest Reqs: Promathia Mission 3-3' has no slot in the schema and no observable predicate -- the Previous field is empty -- so it gates nothing here and is flagged instead. Bullet 10 is pure routing back to the stairwell and merges into the green-door step. The Diremite Assaulters by the Avatar Gate aggro to sound but nothing asks you to kill them, so they are a note and not mobs; recording them would put a sword glyph on a step that is a cutscene.

STAGE D: demoted to medium. The ladder survives every attack -- three evidence points each obtained at its own step and none of them the 3,500 gil reward, both unnamed doors correctly left targetless, the Diremite Assaulters correctly not recorded as mobs, and bullet 14's 'optional exit' sub-bullet correctly kept out of the ladder -- but 'Quest Reqs: Promathia Mission 3-3' is a hard prerequisite with an empty Previous field and no observable predicate, so nothing withholds this quest from a player who cannot accept it. A flag is not a tier; the guide puts 'the ladder is right but a gate is unmodellable' at medium.

steps.note: in the Temple of the Goddess. Pearl if you have cleared Darkness Named, armlet if you have not; the page says the quest runs the same either way, so the two are alternates rather than an AND-list.

the step is placed where you act -- the tower at (G-9) in Beaucedine Glacier -- rather than on the far side of the zone line. The Survival Guide (Fauregandi) is the closest quick travel; the Lv.125 Unity Warp lands at (I-9) on the ramp a level below the tower.
up the stairs, in the small room. The doors seal the instant the pair pops and reopen only when both are dead.
both switch between physical and magical immunity at will, glowing blue or yellow as they change
the same ??? again, once both NMs are down

down the stairs to the blue door, which opens only for the bracelet. The page never names the door -- 'a blue door' is all it says -- so there is no target to mark. It also warns that the blue and green lights above the doorways can look alike depending on your screen settings.
drop down the hole first. Same sealed-room behaviour as the first pair.
the page says they have the exact same immunity switching as Iota and Kappa
the same ??? again, after the NMs

back up to the stairwell room at (I-8), then down the hall where the Blue bracelet was, to the green door on the right; it opens for the Green bracelet. Bullet 10 is only the route back: south into the circular basement room and follow the right wall to the stairs at (G-7), or warp out and re-enter from the Beaucedine Glacier tower at (G-9). The door is neither named nor gridded, so the step sits on the stairwell grid the page does give.

it raises a set of platforms on the floor below for 120 seconds, so everything after it is timed: back down the hall, through the hole at (H-9) marked 'Drop B', west then north across the platform room, up the stairs at (G-7) to the elevator at (H-8)

down the elevator, west side of the circular room; the cutscene is the point of the whole quest. The page grids the elevator at (H-8) but never grids the gate on the floor below, so this step has no grid. Diremite Assaulters down there aggro to sound even at 99 but nothing requires killing them, so they are not recorded as mobs. Opposite the gate, a hall north to a glowing platform teleports you back to the Beaucedine Glacier tower at (G-9).

notes:
Five steps out of eleven bullets, and the largest judgement is what the Burning Circle is doing on this page. Bullet 4's sub-bullet 'Trade the Testimony to Burning Circle' and the whole of bullet 5 -- the assigned-arena table -- are about REMATCHES on later jobs, not about this quest, which is not repeatable and completes exactly once. On a first run Maat takes the testimony and warps you in himself; the page's own 2026 note says it is precisely the warp that stops happening once this is not your first Maat fight. So there is no Burning Circle step: a zone-less Burning Circle would draw a marker in every BCNM zone the player ever stands in, for a path this quest never takes. The arena list is kept in the fight step's note where it is useful.

The job gate is the fifteen pre-Treasures-of-Aht-Urhgan jobs. Bullet 1 says the limit break 'only applies to jobs before the Treasures of Aht Urhgan expansion' and points post-ToAU jobs elsewhere, and the testimony table lists exactly those fifteen and no others. That is a real gate and not the 'a job at level 30+' shape the guide warns about -- a level 70 Blue Mage genuinely cannot do this. The level gate is 66; the 66-70 window's upper end is only the cap this quest raises, so nothing models it.

The testimony is the best observable in the quest and the reason the middle step exists at all: fifteen ALTERNATES, any one held. It must not be an AND-list -- you need your own job's, and which job that is cannot be known from here. The same fifteen are the requirement on the trade to Maat, and the page never names a drop monster or a zone for any of them (it links out to fifteen separate pages), so no mob and no zone is recorded on that step.

Winning gives the title 'Maat Masher' and a Scroll of Instant Warp. The scroll is deliberately NOT evidence: it is an ordinary consumable a player may already be carrying, and the page proves the case itself when it notes a Thief who already owns one cannot steal another. The fight step has no zone for the same reason the arena is unmodellable. Medium overall: the ladder is right, but the arena branch and the 66-70 window are both gates nothing here can express.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 4: so the step carries no zone.

steps.note: on a level 66-70 main job; he asks for that job's testimony. Bullet 1 is scope rather than an action: this limit break exists only for the fifteen jobs that predate Treasures of Aht Urhgan.

bullet 3 is a table of fifteen links, one per job, each pointing at its own page for which monsters drop it and where -- so no monster and no zone can honestly be recorded here. Holding any single testimony satisfies the step, which is why all fifteen are alternates rather than an AND-list.
he asks if you are ready; answering yes teleports you to the arena on a first fight. A testimony survives three attempts before it tears and has to be farmed again.

The arena is fixed per job Balga's Dais for MNK/WHM/SMN, Horlais Peak for WAR/BLM/RNG, Qu'Bia Arena for PLD/DRK/BRD, Waughroon Shrine for RDM/THF/BST, Chamber of Oracles for SAM/NIN/DRG One on one, ten minute limit; Asuran Fists from about five minutes in. Entering strips your support job, every buff except food, and your TP; Maat takes your main job with what looks like a Monk sub, all its abilities and spells, and your SP. The Rhapsody in Umber key item allows Trusts. Two jobs have a second win condition: White Mage can pull him and simply survive five minutes, Thief can steal a Scroll of Instant Warp off him. Winning gives the title Maat Masher and a Scroll of Instant Warp not used as evidence, see the quest note.

the page warns that as of 2026 he may have no post-win dialogue except at the sixth win (the Trust) and for Maat's Cap. You keep the testimony after the fight, and the page's closing note says it can still be traded under the advanced path if you have not opened Aht Urhgan Whitegate through The Road to Aht Urhgan.
